_comment: AGENT: always read this file via the task-index-manager skill before reading or writing any task state. System tracker for ai-worldbuilder (ADR 002). Never add tasks for individual worlds here

tasks.title: Concurrent cell prepares keep invalidating each other's readiness validation
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (design choice). Seen 2026-10-31 on Portswood Rec (53,-42) with neighbour sessions preparing 52,-42/52,-43: `prepare --apply` on one cell changed the readiness revision of neighbouring cells, so a separate prepare then apply was refused 'validation stale' four times; builders had to chain prepare && apply in one shell command. Revision = content_id([POLICY, facts revision, plan_identity]) in lib/journal/cell_readiness.py; I did not find which input changes (suspect vector-map extract rewrite or neighbour plan notes). Questions: should validation of cell A depend on neighbour state at all? Should apply refresh validation itself under the lock? Decide, then fix.

tasks.title: prepare --apply records a duplicate plan_feature on every run (ambiguous legacy plan warning)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. On 53,-42 repeated `prepare --apply` added a second plan `houses_brickfield_road` for the same 6 houses already planned as houses_brickfield_road_w176633174, with warning 'ambiguous legacy plan ... no readable handoff spec'; a duplicate `houses_kitchener_road` (bare id from the 2026-10-29 build in row -43) also showed planned in 53,-42. I dismissed both with dismiss-feature. Decide whether prepare should skip groups already covered by a spec-backed plan, and how legacy bare ids should be matched.

tasks.title: Feature builds across a cell edge silently invalidate a finished neighbour and may generate ghost cells
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT (policy). Applying houses_kitchener_road_w176634502 (footprint z -5382..-5343) reached 5 blocks into finished cell 53,-43 and marked its trees/decor stale (trees=False, decor=False). An earlier apply also generated a lidar ghost cell at 56,-40 (230k blocks, 'ghost-ground' journal seq 620) that the user did not ask for. Decide: warn/confirm before an apply touches a done neighbour; keep or drop frontier ghost generation on feature applies; whether edge fringe (roof overhang) should invalidate trees/decor at all.

tasks.title: World provider osm_extract.py: ogr2ogr ran without OSM_CONFIG_FILE; duplicates lib/sources
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT. In worlds/southampton-build/providers/geofabrik-hampshire/osm_extract.py run_ogr2ogr passed no --config OSM_CONFIG_FILE, so GDAL 3.13's default schema (no `amenity` on points) failed the furniture preset and blocked `prepare --apply`. I patched it in the world checkout (osm_config(): world downloads/osmconf.ini else TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini); the patch is uncommitted and has no test, on top of the owner's existing uncommitted edits. The world provider duplicates the presets and run_ogr2ogr in lib/sources/geofabrik_provider.py; decide whether to delete the copy and call the tool one. Also: manifest hints from prepare (`ref_manifest.py add ...` for prepared-53--42 and prepared-54--42, 52,-42, 52,-43) were not run.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Per-class setting for aerial paving that is not on a mapped way
tasks.notes: Cause (verified in the 63,-45 ground report: 1,107 columns): aerial paving detection turns shade, brown undergrowth and worn grass in park, rural and natural land into light_gray_concrete (ground_layer.classify, the elif a in ('light','dark') branch, about line 523). Deliverable: per-class surface.unmapped_paving (dirt for park, grass for rural and natural): a paving-by-aerial column not on a mapped way (vmap.pri < 40) takes the class kind, and grass inside wood or scrub polygons. This task owns the schema pattern: add the key to the land_use.py validator (which rejects unknown keys) and config/land-use-classes.json; later tasks that add keys (trees, ground_texture) build on it. Test: shade fixture in a park, a rural and a residential class. Check: re-run ground on 63,-45: no light_gray_concrete off mapped ways and the report counts aerial paving as 0 outside residential. Source: docs/plans/park-rural.md.

tasks.title: Trees only from mapped trees, wood, scrub or lidar height on open grass
tasks.notes: Cause: the texture-only crown detector and the dense fill plant meadow and pasture as forest (trees_layer.planning_inputs, dense fill, mosaic detector). Deliverable: on open-land classes keep crowns only from mapped trees, tree rows (#157), wood or scrub within 2 blocks, or lidar standing height of 2 m or more; add a trees.sources key to the class table via the schema pattern from the unmapped-paving task. Reference rule: variant B in docs/plans/park-rural.md (the prototype was scratch, not in the repo). Check: farmland cell 87,-48 has no crowns on open pasture (trial dropped 258 crowns in the park, 186 on farmland); meadow-polygon fixture test passes.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes: Deliverable: inside wood polygons, fill towards the aerial canopy cover (about 80%), mixed species and heights, understorey bushes (persistent leaves at Y+1 to Y+2) and ferns, podzol/coarse_dirt/moss_block floor with grass at the edges; labelled inference, removable through the foliage and decor masks. Owner: trees need more density. Feasibility risk: trees apply cost 962 s for 113 trees (about 8.5 s per tree), so an 80% fill is thousands of trees; diagnose the per-tree apply cost first or batch it. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game.

tasks.title: Rough grass and mottled ground on non-lawn grass
tasks.notes: Owner request: plain grass on farmland reads bland, the aerial shows mottled ground. Deliverable: new class key ground_texture (add to the validator via the schema pattern). Gate: meadow, farmland, grassland, heath, scrub and nature_reserve only; lawns never (rules in docs/plans/park-rural.md section Rough grass without spoiling lawns). Place from aerial texture variance, seeded per cell and column, removable through the masks and counted in the report. Planting is null when frontage.inference is false and rural has inference false, so use its own key; reuse the flower vocabulary of #266 (REFINE_PLANTS), do not re-implement. OWNER DECISION PENDING: palette shares (starting values in the plan doc, low confidence). Check: farmland cell 87,-48 shows tufts and mottling, park lawns unchanged; owner verdict.

tasks.title: Spike: first-return lidar for canopy (Defra first-return DSM)
tasks.notes: Cause: the last-return composite (lidar_composite_last_return_dsm) misses most canopy, so lidar standing height cannot confirm trees. UNVERIFIED: that Defra publishes a first-return DSM; config/system-providers.json lists only ukdefra-lidar and ukdefra-dsm. Deliverable: an evaluate-data-source write-up (coverage, licence, cost on the wire, whether it exists as a download) and a go or no-go; add-data-source only on go. Used by the tree gate once present. Check: findings in docs/plans/ with a verdict; if go, canopy height read on a wood cell.

tasks.title: Rivers across cells: per-cell clipped water bodies
tasks.notes: Cause (verified): water_body items carry one cells entry and propose takes one cell, building the body whole; the Itchen spans 12 cells and 22,824 columns. The trial used a scratch clip wrapper and a manual plan_feature note. Deliverable: build per cell, clipped, no bank ring on clip edges, plan recorded per cell. Same edge policy as blocked task 234 (building across a cell edge). Test on a two-cell fixture. Check: Itchen reach across 63,-45 and its neighbour joins without a seam or bank wall. Water level along the reach is a separate task.

tasks.title: Park bench inference placed nothing: decide class precedence for furniture
tasks.notes: Cause (from the 63,-45 decor report): ways_skipped 'no bench density for the adjoining class' 5, 0 candidates. Hypothesis, not verified: land_class_columns uses the smallest-polygon rule, so a path through meadow or beside wood classes as rural or natural and only the park row has bench_per_100m (config/land-use-classes.json, used in lib/layers/decor_plan.py, BENCH_PATHS footway, path, pedestrian). Owner choice needed: should a path inside a leisure=park polygon take park furniture when the nearer polygon is meadow or wood? Deliverable: check the five ways' classes, then change adjoining_class or the class precedence, or record the rule. Check: named test; re-run on 63,-45 gives benches at the stated density.

tasks.title: Spike: tree lines along hedges and lanes that OSM does not map
tasks.notes: Mapped natural=tree_row is already read (#157) and the tree gate must keep it. Gap: hedgerow tree lines and tree belts that are not mapped are lost by the open-land gate. Deliverable: findings in docs/plans/ on whether aerial plus lidar evidence along mapped hedges and lanes can place them, with a go or no-go. Check: the hedge on 87,-48 and the unmapped north-east tree belt in that cell get trees from evidence in the prototype.

tasks.title: Lidar outbuilding candidates must not be proposed on mapped water
tasks.notes: Cause: _outbuilding_items in lib/layers/decor_plan.py does not put water columns in lidar_items(exclude=...). place_outbuildings already refuses water columns when applying, so nothing was built; the garage at (8117,-5733) in the Itchen shows as unresolved. Deliverable: exclude mapped water columns when proposing. Check: unit test; 63,-45 decor report has no outbuilding-lidar-8117-m5733 in unresolved_items.

tasks.title: Widen a mapped path to the paving seen beside it
tasks.notes: Cause partly unverified: the riverside path in 63,-45 has est_width 1.75 and surface asphalt, and the aerial width was lost, so it reads as a coarse-dirt band with a thin grey strip (owner noted this as a fault). Deliverable: widen a mapped way to the paving seen beside it in the aerial, per class. Check: in game the riverside path in cell 63,-45 reads as one path of the aerial width.

tasks.title: River water level from lidar along the reach
tasks.notes: Today one integer water level per body. Deliverable: sample the level from lidar along the reach so a long river steps with the terrain. Split from the per-cell rivers task. Check: the Itchen reach across two cells has no stranded water or dry bed in game.

tasks.title: Dressing must not write ground-layer work onto a cell with no real ground pass
tasks.notes: Cause (found with the owner in trial #258): class dressing wrote white_concrete car-park bay lines (a ground-layer marking, craftsmanship section 3a) onto cell 50,-35 of southampton-build, which had only ghost ground. The throwaway car_park() clipped to a box spanning two cells and gated only on the approved-cell list; the approval for that cell covered buildings and ghost ground, not the ground layer. Deliverable: dressing and any pass that writes ground-layer things must refuse, or run the ground pass first, on a cell without real ground; cell approvals say which layers they cover. Check: test with a ghost-only cell: dressing refuses and writes nothing; cell 50,-35's lines resolved by the owner's choice (ground pass there, or removed).

tasks.title: Group touching non-house buildings into one feature candidate
tasks.notes: Cause (verified): cell_features._package_unbuilt emits one candidate per non-house way and only houses are grouped, via _split_runs. Readiness already counts every ref a spec lists under ways (task 293, lib/journal/plan_refs.py), so the gap is the candidate and the plan id. JOIN_GAP is 12 blocks and would chain a whole estate; the trial's sheds were separated by walls. Deliverable: in lib/journal/cell_features.py group non-house candidates of the same building= tag whose footprints touch (gap 1 block or less) into one candidate of a new kind (group) with all its refs; plan id is the lowest ref, as for split house groups in plan_ids_for_candidates; a spec naming that id and listing the refs in ways covers all of them. Check: Belgrave 55,-41 proposes the west shed (units 1-4) and the east shed (units 7-18) as two candidates, not 20; fixture test: two touching retail ways give one candidate and a distant third stays single; a group crossing a cell edge is planned once (drop_covered_candidates). Unverified: whether the owner wants groups per structure only or also per parade. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.title: Evidence revision must not hash build specs
tasks.notes: Cause (read from code, not yet confirmed as the trial's exact trigger): LocalEvidence.source_revision() in lib/journal/readiness_evidence.py hashes every json/png under the world's config/, reference/ and site/builds/, so every new or changed build spec changes the evidence revision of every cell: landing a feature stales its neighbours (the trial re-ran prepare --evidence-only by hand; the sheds and Westquay neighbours went stale). Probably also the unexplained cause in blocked task #232 ('did not find which input changes'); relates to #234, do not set blockedBy. The site/builds hash was added in 88ac28d with no recorded reason; spec content is already covered by plan identity and plan_refs. Deliverable: drop site/builds from source_revision (evidence only). Confirm first by diffing revision_parts before and after a spec write. Check: test: write a spec under site/builds, evidence revisions of other cells do not change; live: apply a feature crossing into 51,-36 straight after another landed, with no 'evidence facts changed' refusal and no manual prepare. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.title: Industrial and big-box street-face rules by land-use class
tasks.notes: Owner accepted the industrial and big-box defaults in game (Belgrave 55,-41; Westquay South 43,-16, roof excluded). The prototype dress.py is not in the repo; nothing for shutters, fascia, bay marks or name signs exists in lib. The unwanted window grid is real: Builder.windows in lib/builds/feature_build.py falls to DIRECTIONS on all faces when facade_plan has no glazing. Deliverable: a shared front-column helper (a column whose outside neighbour is nearer the mapped street line, excluding side, alley and party walls); industrial shutter, fascia and bay marks with no storey window grid; big-box glazed base, fascia and name sign (no roof). Keyed by land-use class, UK-wide. Files: lib/builds/feature_build.py, lib/builds/facade_plan.py, lib/sources/land_use.py, config/land-use-classes.json. Relates to blocked spike #257 (file implementation after its findings; the owner has already accepted these two classes). Check: rebuild Belgrave 55,-41 and Westquay 43,-16 from rules only, no scratch script; owner verdict in game. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.title: Shop street-face rules by shop kind
tasks.notes: Deliverable: glass, door at pavement level, fascia, contrasting wrapped name sign, and continuous awning by shop kind (cafe/restaurant/fast_food/food), applied to the street face only, never to side or alley walls or walls abutting another building, using the front-column helper from the industrial and big-box task. Owner verdict on v2: better but not accepted as default. Fixes issues I-051 (shop front wraps onto party/side walls: snags S-091, S-094) and I-050 (floating trapdoors at y=41, S-090) when landed; log each fix with issues.py fix and a check line per snag. Relates to #257. Check: Daily Echo and October Books in 50,-36 after a rebuild have no front on side walls and no trapdoor above y 40; owner verdict. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.title: Fit straight runs to stepped shop fronts so awnings, signs and doors attach
tasks.notes: Owner: square off shop fronts; awnings on angled walls leave gaps to the wall and signs hover; the door near Dido's is not fully framed (door jamb rule _door_jambs_solid assumes a straight run); the Admiral side is a mess. Same cause: items placed one block out from a stepped face. Deliverable: fit straight runs to the stepped front columns and place glass, door, fascia, sign and awning on the run line, filling stair-step gaps so awnings and signs touch the wall (owner: better thick than gaps) and doors on stepped faces get full jambs. Fixes I-052 (awnings leave gaps, S-093) when landed; log the fix with a check line per snag. Check: Admiral and Dido's fronts in 50,-36: no hovering sign, awning touches the wall, the door near Dido's fully framed, no trapdoor above y 40; owner verdict. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.title: Shop typology: terrace-house body over a shopfront ground floor
tasks.notes: Owner: west-side shops are three storeys with a dormer top floor, east-side shops two storeys with an upper bay window and pitched roofs, not flat commercial. This is the question blocked spike #257 asks, so file work only after its findings (blockedBy 257); alternative is to add the owner's west/east evidence to #257. Deliverable: storeys and dormers from lidar eave and ridge, pitched roofs, upper bay windows, reusing the terrace builder (scripts/house_build.py). Check: west and east parades of 50,-36 show dormers and bay windows by side; owner verdict. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.notes: Owner noted little street furniture where the street has traffic lights, but the trial did not run decor, so that observation is unverified. Real gap: EXTRACT_JOBS in lib/sources/street_furniture.py omits highway=traffic_signals and crossing, and those kinds do not exist. Deliverable: add traffic_signals and crossing kinds (extract preset, recipe, decor placement); traffic island only where mapped. Run decor on 50,-36 first to see what is already missing. Depends in practice on blocked #237 (furniture preset fails under default GDAL) if that is still the case. Check: decor dry run on 50,-36 lists signals at the OSM signal nodes. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md (trial #258).

tasks.notes: Owner: the 'church' on the high street was an old bingo hall with a big facade, steps and a permanent awning; street view would have shown it. Tier A is owner-nominated in docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md section 2. tasks.title: Big-box roof follows the aerial (spike first)
tasks.notes: Owner: Westquay South roof does not match the aerial (long PV rows on a flat light roof; the prototype's central grid of detectors did not). tasks.title: Surface car parks paint as tarmac in the ground layer
tasks.notes: Cause (reported by trial #258 from the 50,-35 ground pass, not independently verified): the ground layer does not read amenity=parking (surface car parks) as a surface, because land-use classes are kept out of ground paint (task #158 keeps landuse=residential, retail, commercial, industrial unread so they never paint under houses). So a car park comes out as aerial-coloured grass and tarmac patches: 50,-35 plan was tarmac 2,060, paving 3,493, forecourt 1,283, grass 2,728 columns, and the owner saw grass in a car park where the aerial shows none (issue I-054, snag S-096). Deliverable: ground layer maps amenity=parking (surface, and not multi-storey or underground) to tarmac, with bay lines left to task 336; a narrow exception to the #158 rule recorded in the rules and the land-use notes. Check: re-run ground on 50,-35 (needs the surface-probe fix #315 first, or the cell reads as empty below Y 31): the car park behind the high street is tarmac with no grass patches; a fixture test with an amenity=parking polygon and one with a multi-storey parking polygon. Source: docs/plans/industrial-commercial.md section 8.
